evals.query: Add Micrometer metrics to my Kora 2.0 Java service and expose them for Prometheus scraping.
expected_behavior: Adds io.koraframework:micrometer-module and io.koraframework:http-server-undertow with the io.koraframework:kora-bom BOM at koraVersion=2.0.0.RC2 from mavenCentral(), plus annotationProcessor "io.koraframework:annotation-processors"
Extends MetricsModule (io.koraframework.micrometer.module) on the @KoraApp interface alongside UndertowPublicHttpServerModule

Sets httpServer.telemetry.metrics.enabled = true in application.conf and explains that TelemetryConfig.MetricsConfig.enabled() defaults to false in Kora 2.0, so without it no http_server_* metric is ever recorded
Configures the scrape endpoint under httpServer.system (system.port, system.metricsPath), not on the public port
Does not add io.micrometer:micrometer-registry-prometheus separately, since micrometer-module already brings it
Uses no ru.tinkoff.kora coordinates, no kora-parent BOM, no UndertowHttpServerModule, and no privateApiHttpPort / privateApiHttpMetricsPath keys

evals.query: Set up Prometheus metrics in my Kora 2.0 Kotlin service.
expected_behavior: Uses ksp("io.koraframework:symbol-processors") rather than an annotation processor, with the io.koraframework:kora-bom platform at koraVersion=2.0.0.RC2
Extends MetricsModule and UndertowPublicHttpServerModule on the @KoraApp interface, entry point KoraApplication.run(ApplicationGraph::graph)
Sets httpServer.telemetry.metrics.enabled = true and explains the false default
Injects MeterRegistry through the constructor of a @Component (io.koraframework.common.annotation.Component)
Uses no suspend functions, Mono/Flux or CompletionStage — Kora 2.0 contracts are synchronous

evals.query: I added MetricsModule and my Kora 2.0 service starts fine. GET http://localhost:8085/metrics returns 200 and I can see jvm_memory_used_bytes and kora_up, but there is no http_server_request_duration at all. Is metrics collection broken?
expected_behavior: Identifies the cause immediately: TelemetryConfig.MetricsConfig.enabled() defaults to false in Kora 2.0, so component metrics are off even though the registry is bound

Fixes it with httpServer { telemetry.metrics.enabled = true } and notes the same flag is needed per component (httpClient.<name>, jdbc, grpcServer, scheduling.telemetry, resilient.telemetry, cache/Kafka config paths)
Explains that this fails silently — no warning is logged, the endpoint still answers 200, and JVM meters still appear, which is exactly why it looks like it is working
Does not suggest that metrics are enabled by default, and does not offer the global metrics.enabled key as the fix — it already defaults to true and is a kill switch that enables no component metric
Does not recommend adding a separate registry dependency or an external actuator framework

evals.query: My Kora 2.0 application.conf has httpServer.telemetry.metrics.enabled = true and jdbc.telemetry.metrics.enabled = true, but /metrics answers 200 with the single line '# Metric Scraper disabled'. The config key is definitely set.
expected_behavior: Recognises '# Metric Scraper disabled' as MetricsHandler's response when no MetricsScraper is present in the graph, which means MetricsModule is not on the @KoraApp interface

Explains the second gate: every telemetry factory computes metricEnabled = meterRegistry != null && config.metrics().enabled(), and MeterRegistry is injected as @Nullable, so the config flag alone is inert
Fixes it by adding MetricsModule (and the io.koraframework:micrometer-module dependency) — not by changing the config
Notes that a 200 from /metrics proves nothing, because MetricsHandler returns 200 in every branch
Does not claim the endpoint is missing or return a 404 diagnosis

evals.query: My Prometheus scrape config points at http://order-service:8080/metrics and gets a 404. My Kora 2.0 application.conf has httpServer.privateApiHttpPort = 9090 and httpServer.privateApiHttpMetricsPath = "/metrics". Why is the endpoint missing?
expected_behavior: Explains that /metrics is served by MetricsHandler on the SYSTEM server, never on the public one — the public port only serves @HttpController routes
Identifies privateApiHttpPort and privateApiHttpMetricsPath as removed Kora 1.x keys that are unrecognised HOCON keys in 2.0, ignored without any warning
Renames them to httpServer.system.port and httpServer.system.metricsPath
Points out the consequence of the silent fallback: the system server actually came up on its default 8085, not on the configured 9090, so the scrape target is wrong too
Points the scrape target at httpServer.system.port
Does not invent a config key that moves /metrics onto the public port

evals.query: Write an integration test for my Kora 2.0 service that verifies metrics are actually being collected.
expected_behavior: Asserts on the /metrics response BODY, not only on the 200 status code, and says why: MetricsHandler returns 200 in every branch, including when no MetricsScraper exists
Drives real traffic through the public port first, then asserts the body contains http_server_request_duration or http_server_active_requests
Asserts the body does not contain '# Metric Scraper disabled'
Uses the system port (httpServer.system.port, default 8085) for the /metrics request and the public port for the traffic
Enables telemetry.metrics.enabled = true in the test configuration, including inside any KoraConfigModification.ofString(...) HOCON block
Does not treat the presence of jvm_* or kora_up as evidence that component metrics work

evals.query: Tracing is enabled by default in Kora 2.0, so my /metrics and /system/readiness calls should be producing spans — but I see none for them. Everything else is traced.
expected_behavior: Explains that the tracing default of true does NOT hold under httpServer.system: SystemHttpServerConfig.SystemHttpServerTelemetryConfig.SystemHttpServerTracingConfig overrides enabled() to false
Notes this is deliberate — scrapes and probes would otherwise flood the trace backend with one span per interval
Shows httpServer.system.telemetry.tracing.enabled = true as the explicit opt-in if it is genuinely wanted
Correctly states that metrics and logging default to false everywhere, including the system server, while tracing defaults to true everywhere else
Does not claim tracing is globally disabled or that a tracing exporter is missing

evals.query: Create a Kora 2.0 Java service that records how long user creation takes and counts created users by email provider.
expected_behavior: Injects MeterRegistry through the constructor of an io.koraframework.common.annotation.Component
Registers the Timer once in the constructor with serviceLevelObjectives(Duration...) buckets
Caches Counter instances per provider with ConcurrentHashMap.computeIfAbsent so the email.provider tag stays bounded
Maps the raw email domain onto a bounded set with a safe fallback such as "unknown" or "other", rather than tagging with the raw domain
States that custom meters need MetricsModule only and are not gated by telemetry.metrics.enabled — that flag governs Kora's own component instrumentation
Does not use field injection, @Autowired, or ru.tinkoff.kora imports

evals.query: Add a business metric to my Kora 2.0 Kotlin service that measures order processing latency and counts orders by payment provider.
expected_behavior: Uses io.koraframework.common.annotation.Component with constructor injection of MeterRegistry
Builds the meters in property initialisers or init, not on every call
Caches meters per bounded tag value with ConcurrentHashMap.computeIfAbsent
Handles the Kotlin specifics: DistributionSummary.record takes a Double, and Timer.record needs a disambiguated overload (Supplier { } or recordCallable) when the lambda returns a value
Writes a plain synchronous function — no suspend, Flow, Mono or CompletionStage

evals.query: Attach common tags (service, environment, version) to every metric in my Kora 2.0 app.
expected_behavior: Puts static common tags in the global metrics.tags map (io.koraframework.micrometer.module.MetricsConfig, top-level config path metrics) and/or a MetricsTagsProvider @Component for values computed at startup

Explains that MetricsModule's commonTagsMeterRegistryInitializer merges every MetricsTagsProvider with metrics.tags into one MeterFilter.commonTags(...), with metrics.tags applied last so config wins on a key conflict
Notes the tags land on every meter in the registry, JVM meters and kora_up included, and that the values must stay bounded

If it shows a custom PrometheusMeterRegistryInitializer, says it runs alongside the common-tags initializer (not a @DefaultComponent since RC2, #935), so it must not re-merge metrics.tags itself, and must return the registry
May contrast it with the per-component telemetry.metrics.tags config key
Does not invent a MeterRegistryCustomizer, @Default annotation or any external customizer type

evals.query: Which metric and labels does Kora 2.0 emit for HTTP server request latency, and how do I query the error rate in Prometheus?
expected_behavior: Names http.server.request.duration as a Timer registered by DefaultHttpServerMetricsFactory, plus http.server.active_requests as a Gauge
Lists the real 2.0 tags: server.name, server.port, http.request.method, http.response.status_code, http.route, url.scheme, server.address, error.type
Writes the 5xx error-rate query against http_response_status_code=~"5.." on the _count series, and may add error_type!="" for requests that ended in an exception
Notes that http.server.active_requests carries no status code, because the request is still in flight
Does not invent http.server.requests, labels named status or route, or the 1.x metrics.opentelemetrySpec switch

evals.query: I am porting a Grafana dashboard from Kora 1.x to Kora 2.0. It uses db_client_request_duration, cache_duration, messaging_receive_duration for Kafka and s3_client_duration. Which of these still work?
expected_behavior: Says none of the four are correct for Kora 2.0 and gives the current meters: db.client.operation.duration, cache.operation.duration, messaging.process.duration (Kafka consumer), rpc.client.call.duration with rpc.system.name = s3
Notes that messaging.process.duration is shared with the JMS consumer, so the Kafka query filters by messaging_system="kafka"
Flags the database tag renames: db.client.connection.pool.name, db.system.name, db.query.text, db.operation.name
Warns that S3, SOAP and gRPC clients share the meter name rpc.client.call.duration and must be separated by the rpc_system_name label
Mentions that rpc.*.requests_per_rpc and responses_per_rpc no longer exist in 2.0
Tells the user to read the exact exported series names from a running /metrics rather than assuming the suffix

evals.query: Configure latency histogram buckets in Kora 2.0 so I can compute p95 and p99 for the HTTP server and for my own API timer.
expected_behavior: For Kora's own meters, sets httpServer.telemetry.metrics.slo as an array and notes that bare numbers are milliseconds while strings accept "250ms" / "1s"
Notes that slo has a 14-entry default (MetricsConfig.DEFAULT_SLO, 1 ms to 90 s) and that setting enabled = true is still required for the buckets to be produced at all
For custom meters, uses Timer.builder(...).serviceLevelObjectives(Duration.ofMillis(...), ...)
Explains that buckets let Prometheus compute quantiles with histogram_quantile, while publishPercentiles computes them in-process, costs CPU and does not aggregate across instances
Mentions that each bucket boundary multiplies the series count per tag combination
Keeps the metrics endpoint on the system port

evals.query: How do I switch my Kora metrics to the newer OpenTelemetry naming convention? I currently have metrics { opentelemetrySpec = "V120" } in my config.
expected_behavior: States that metrics.opentelemetrySpec does not exist in Kora 2.0: the global metrics section maps onto io.koraframework.micrometer.module.MetricsConfig, which declares only enabled and tags
Explains that 2.0 emits one fixed naming scheme, corresponding to what 1.x called V123, so the switch has no purpose
Tells the user to delete the key, warning that as an unrecognised HOCON key it is ignored without a warning and gives a false sense that it is doing something
Notes that several meter names changed on top of that scheme, so the 1.x V123 metric list still cannot be reused verbatim
Does not invent a replacement key or a semantic-convention version setting

evals.query: Can I push Kora 2.0 metrics directly to Datadog or an OTLP endpoint from the application?
expected_behavior: Explains that micrometer-module is Prometheus pull-only and serves /metrics on the system HTTP server
States there is no Kora configuration to swap the registry for a push exporter
Recommends scraping /metrics with an agent (Prometheus, OpenTelemetry Collector prometheus receiver, vmagent, Datadog OpenMetrics check) and forwarding from there
Distinguishes metric export from trace export, which is configured separately under tracing.exporter by opentelemetry-tracing-exporter-grpc/-http

May mention that the registry and the MetricsScraper are @DefaultComponent and can be replaced by a @Component, and that a non-Prometheus registry without a matching MetricsScraper yields a 200 with an empty body
Does not fabricate micrometer.statsd, micrometer.otlp or metrics.export.* config keys

evals.query: My Kora 2.0 service has jdbc.telemetry.metrics.driverMetrics = true but no hikaricp_ series show up in /metrics. driverMetrics defaults to true anyway, so what is wrong?
expected_behavior: Identifies the missing jdbc.telemetry.metrics.enabled = true

Explains the mechanism: with enabled = false the factory returns NoopDatabaseTelemetry, whose meterRegistry() is the NoopMeterRegistry, and JdbcDataSource passes exactly that registry to dataSource.setMetricRegistry(...) — so Hikari records into a registry that discards everything
Confirms driverMetrics does default to true for JDBC and Cassandra, but false for Kafka consumers and publishers
Does not suggest adding a Hikari or Micrometer dependency

evals.query: Review this Kora metrics code that adds userId and requestId as tags on a counter and tell me what is wrong.
expected_behavior: Identifies userId and requestId as unbounded high-cardinality tags that grow the registry without limit and leak memory
Recommends bounded values instead: http.request.method, the http.route template, error.type, or an aggregated dimension such as a user tier
Suggests caching meters per bounded value with computeIfAbsent, while warning that caching an unbounded key only moves the leak
May note that per-request attribution belongs in logs or traces, not in metrics, since every label combination is retained forever
May reference Kora's own approach: route templates with an UNKNOWN_ROUTE fallback, query ids instead of SQL text, and exception classes instead of messages
Does not recommend an external actuator or tracing framework as the fix

evals.query: Add a readiness probe to my Kora 2.0 service that reports not-ready while the reference-data cache is warming up, and wire the Kubernetes probes.
expected_behavior: Implements io.koraframework.common.readiness.ReadinessProbe with @Nullable ReadinessProbeFailure probe(), returning null when ready and new ReadinessProbeFailure("...") when not
Registers it as an io.koraframework.common.annotation.Component so All<PromiseOf<ReadinessProbe>> collects it
Points the Kubernetes probes at httpServer.system.port with paths /system/liveness and /system/readiness
Does not use the 1.x API: no ru.tinkoff.kora.http.server.common.ReadinessProbe, no check() method, no Result.success() / Result.failure(...)
May note that the failure message is returned in the 503 response body, that a 30 s aggregate cap applies, and that JDBC already ships a readiness probe behind jdbc.readinessProbe (default false)

evals.query: Our Kora 2.0 service answers 200 on GET :8085/metrics but the body is completely empty — not even kora_up or jvm_* series. httpServer.telemetry.metrics.enabled = true is set, MetricsModule is on the @KoraApp, and the shared base config has metrics { enabled = false }.
expected_behavior: Identifies the global metrics.enabled = false as the cause: MetricsModule.prometheusMeterRegistry returns NoopMeterRegistry.INSTANCE instead of the PrometheusMeterRegistryWrapper
Explains the empty body: prometheusMetricsScraper only scrapes a PrometheusMeterRegistry and otherwise writes nothing, while MetricsHandler still answers 200
Notes that with the kill switch no JVM binders, no kora_up and no initializers are applied, and that custom meters on the injected MeterRegistry are silently discarded too
Fixes it by removing the key or setting metrics.enabled = true (its default), keeping the per-component telemetry.metrics.enabled = true flags
Distinguishes the global metrics.enabled (default true, kill switch) from <component>.telemetry.metrics.enabled (default false, opt-in)
Does not diagnose it as a missing MetricsModule ('# Metric Scraper disabled' is a different body)

evals.query: In my Kora 2.0 Kotlin service I want every metric tagged with the region read from the REGION environment variable at startup, plus a static service=order-service tag.
expected_behavior: Implements io.koraframework.micrometer.module.MetricsTagsProvider in a @Component class overriding fun tags(): Map<String, String>
Puts service = order-service in the global metrics.tags map in application.conf
States that providers and metrics.tags are merged into one global MeterFilter.commonTags by MetricsModule, config applied last so a key present in both keeps the config value
Notes that tags() is called once during graph initialization, so a value that changes later is not picked up
Falls back to a bounded default (e.g. "unknown") when REGION is unset rather than tagging with null
Does not write a PrometheusMeterRegistryInitializer for this, and does not repeat the tag in every <component>.telemetry.metrics.tags block

evals.query: I set metrics.tags { service = "orders" } in my Kora 2.0.0.RC1 app and it worked. Then I added a @Module with a PrometheusMeterRegistryInitializer that installs a MeterFilter deny rule, and now the service tag is gone from every series. Why, and what do I do on RC2?
expected_behavior: Explains that metrics.tags and MetricsTagsProvider are applied by MetricsModule's commonTagsMeterRegistryInitializer, which was a @DefaultComponent in RC1

Explains that All<PrometheusMeterRegistryInitializer> leaves a @DefaultComponent candidate out when a non-default candidate of the same type exists, so on RC1 the new initializer silently displaced the built-in one

Says the fix is upgrading to 2.0.0.RC2, where #935 made the common-tags initializer a regular component, so the custom initializer keeps only its deny rule and must not re-merge the tags (that installs the filter twice)
Does not claim the deny filter itself removed the tag or that metrics.tags is ignored in general

evals.query: Which metrics does a Kora 2.0 Caffeine @Cache publish when I turn its metrics on, and do I need a workaround for duplicate meter registration?
expected_behavior: Says metrics come on with telemetry.metrics.enabled = true under the @Cache config path, with MetricsModule on the graph
Says Kora's own cache.operation.duration / cache.requests meters are not emitted for Caffeine (only Redis caches record them)

Adds Micrometer's CaffeineCacheMetrics binder meters — cache.gets, cache.puts, cache.evictions, cache.eviction.weight, cache.size — registered once over a recordStats() cache, named by the @Cache config path
States that no workaround is needed: the cache is instrumented through the binder only
Does not suggest a custom CaffeineStatsCounter, disabling the binder, or catching IllegalArgumentException at startup

evals.query: After upgrading Kora 2.0.0.RC1 to RC2 my Grafana panels on rpc_server_duration_seconds_count, cache_ratio_total{type="hit"} and resilient_circuitbreaker_state{name="payments"} are empty. What changed?
expected_behavior: Says RC2 (#972) renamed the meters: rpc.server.duration / rpc.client.duration -> rpc.server.call.duration / rpc.client.call.duration, cache.ratio -> cache.requests

Gives the new tags: rpc.system -> rpc.system.name, rpc.grpc.status_code -> rpc.response.status_code carrying the gRPC status code name (OK, UNAVAILABLE) instead of the number; cache type -> cache.result, origin/operation -> cache.origin/cache.operation
Says every resilience tag is now resilient.-prefixed: resilient_circuitbreaker_state{resilient_name="payments"}
Mentions that the Lettuce completion timer is now db.client.operation.duration with db_system_name="redis" and the JMS consumer timer is messaging.process.duration
Does not suggest a config switch to restore the old names; none exists
